b: Date range is a time dimension in Amazon Ads unified reporting. Added to a report, it labels each row with the first and last day of the period the row's numbers cover, so a row covering November 1 to November 30, 2026 shows impressions, spend and sales totalled for that whole stretch rather than for a single day, week or month. The dimension exists because a report has to declare its own time frame. A table exported without dates is unusable once it leaves the console, and a spreadsheet merging two exports needs a column saying which period each row describes. Date range supplies that column for the coarsest grain Amazon offers, the summary of an entire chosen period.
Where date range sits in the unified report

Amazon's unified reporting dimensions page, a Support Center reference updated on November 11, 2026, lists 156 attributes in 11 categories. The Time category holds eight of them. PPC Land's count shows that all eight carry markers for DVA+, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display, along with the currency, audience, conversion and benchmark fields. DVA+ is Amazon's display, video and audio buying, sold as Amazon DSP (demand-side platform) until September 29, 2026.

The eight time attributes are Date, Week, Day of month, Month, Year, Day of week, Hour and Date range. Most of them slice a period into units. Date range does the opposite: it holds the period together.

The reference also maps each unified field to the names it replaced. Date range takes over from "Interval start date / Interval end date" in the former DSP reports and from "Start Date / End Date" in sponsored ads reports, according to PPC Land's reading of the mapping table.

Amazon's documentation says that "when a dimension does not apply to an ad product, its value appears as null," which is what happens to device type or deal ID on sponsored ads rows. Date range applies everywhere, so every row has a value.
How the period is set and reported
A report is built by choosing a scope, a time grain, dimensions and metrics. The time grain decides how the chosen period is cut up.

Step one is the period. An analyst picks start and end dates in the report builder or sends them in an API request. How far back the period can reach depends on the grain. The November 2025 beta notice gave "two weeks for hourly reporting, 15 months for daily or weekly reporting," and "up to six years for monthly, yearly, or summary-grain reporting." A summary covering an entire calendar year from 2021 is therefore possible; a daily breakdown of the same year is not.

Step two is the grain. At summary grain, the report returns one row per combination of the other dimensions for the whole period. At daily grain, it returns one row per day, labelled by the Date dimension.

Step three is the label. Date range then shows the period's boundaries on each row. A Sponsored Products campaign spends $310 between November 1 and November 30, 2026. A summary report returns one row, with Date range reading November 1 to November 30 and cost of $310. A daily report over the same period returns 30 rows, each carrying a single date and a share of the $310.

Amazon's older API documentation shows the same logic in its field names. Sponsored Products report requests in version 3 of the Amazon Ads Reporting API accept a timeUnit of SUMMARY or DAILY. Summary examples request startDate and endDate columns; the daily example requests date. Those report types allowed a maximum period of 31 days and retained data for 95 days, according to the API guide. The DSP API guide set the same 31-day ceiling, required the end date to fall within the past 90 days, and said SUMMARY aggregates the whole period. Sample DSP rows carry intervalStart and intervalEnd as epoch timestamps in milliseconds, which is where the "Interval start date" name came from.

The label on a row says which days the activity happened, but the sales in that row may not have happened on those days. Amazon's general availability release standardised attribution "from conversion to traffic based," meaning a purchase is credited to the date of the click or view that led to it. A summary row for November 1 to November 30 can therefore include a purchase made on December 12, if the click came on November 28 and the attribution window is 14 days.

The consequence is that a date range ending recently is not final. SellerApp, an Amazon tools vendor, says click data arrives "within 12 hours through the API" and conversion data is "usually available within 24 hours," with figures that "may change during restatement." The same November report run on December 1 and on December 20 will show different sales under an identical Date range value.

Amazon has not published when start and end date fields entered its sponsored ads reports. Intentwise, an agency software company, wrote in April 2023 that sponsored ads data through the API "only went back 60 days" before version 3, which extended Sponsored Products to 95 days.

On the programmatic side, Amazon DSP added a time breakdown to its campaign tables on October 6, 2022, according to Amazon's launch notice, which said customers "can analyze the time series by daily, weekly, monthly and day of week view." Hourly granularity came through a separate channel. When PPC Land covered Amazon Marketing Stream in December 2024, it reported that traffic and conversion data were "summarized hourly", compared with the daily granularity of the reporting API.

Unified reporting brought the pieces into one schema. Amazon opened it in beta on November 11, 2025 with grain-based data windows in place of the old per-request API limits. The same day, Amazon extended the Amazon Marketing Cloud lookback window from 13 to 25 months in the United States and Canada, letting clean-room queries cover two holiday seasons. General availability followed on June 8, 2026, as PPC Land reported when unified reporting exited beta. The dimensions reference published on November 11, 2026 gave the field its current name.

For most advertisers, summary-grain reports are the ones that travel: monthly client decks, quarterly business reviews, invoices reconciled against spend. Date range records which period was summed, so an October summary and a November summary can sit in one spreadsheet without confusion.
The six-year window for summary data also changes year-on-year analysis. Under the old 60-day or 95-day API limits, agencies stored their own history; a multi-year summary can now be pulled directly.

The migration deadline adds urgency. Amazon's legacy report pages become read-only on December 17, 2026 and close on January 31, 2027, when unmigrated reports will be lost. Scheduled reports and API scripts that read "Start Date" and "End Date" or "Interval start date" columns must be remapped to the unified name.

Retention figures conflict. Intentwise put Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display API history at 60 days; SellerApp gives 731 days for Sponsored Brands, matching Amazon's API guide for the purchased product report. Historical exports made under the old limits will not line up neatly with unified ones.

Time zone is not stated. The dimensions reference, as summarised by PPC Land, does not say which clock defines a day's boundaries. For a report spanning accounts in the United States and Germany, it is not documented whether a "day" follows each marketplace's local clock or a single one.

Summaries hide movement. A single row for a 30-day period cannot show that half the spend fell on Black Friday. Return on ad spend over a summary is a ratio of totals, which differs from an average of daily ratios.

The attribution basis shifted mid-history. On January 1, 2026, Amazon replaced view-through attribution for store ads with a "shopping-signal enhanced" last-touch model. A six-year summary therefore mixes two crediting methods, and a date range straddling January 1, 2026 compares unlike quantities unless the "Purchases (all views)" metrics are used.

Sponsored TV coverage is unclear. The reference states "We do not support Streaming TV Smart mode/ Sponsored TV yet," while marking many attributes for Sponsored TV, PPC Land noted. PPC Land's count table gives no Sponsored TV figure for Time.
Date range vs Date. Date labels a single day at daily grain. Date range labels the full period at summary grain.

Date range vs campaign or flight dates. Campaign start date, Campaign end date, Flight start date and Flight end date describe when a campaign or budget segment is scheduled to run. Date range describes the reporting period chosen by the analyst. PPC Land's explainer on the flight covers the scheduling sense.

Date range vs lookback window. A lookback window is "the stretch of time before a conversion during which an earlier click, view or impression stays eligible for credit." It governs which sales are counted; date range governs which days of ad activity are shown.

Amazon updated the unified reporting dimensions reference on November 11, 2026, the page behind PPC Land's count of 156 dimensions. As of November 2026, Date range is one of eight time fields marked for all four core ad products. From January 1, 2027, DVA display impressions are counted only once on screen, a change Amazon expects to cut impression counts by about 63% on average. A summary for December 2026 to January 2027 will contain impressions counted under two definitions.

Who: Amazon Ads defines the dimension; advertisers, agencies, sellers and reporting vendors using Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display and DVA+ use it to label summary reports.

What: Date range is a time dimension that shows the start and end dates of the period a report row covers, replacing the "Start Date / End Date" and "Interval start date / Interval end date" fields of the legacy reports.

When: Unified reporting has carried time dimensions since its beta on November 11, 2025 and general availability on June 8, 2026; the current field list dates from November 11, 2026. Legacy reports close on January 31, 2027.
Where: In the Time category of Amazon Ads unified reporting, in the Ads Console and the Reporting API, with summary-grain data available for up to six years.

Why: A summary row is meaningless without its period. Date range records which days were summed, so exported reports can be compared, joined and reconciled, subject to attribution restatements and Amazon's undocumented handling of time zones.
